working: For every real x, \(x^{2}\ge 0\) and \(3|x|\ge 0\), so \(x^{2}+3|x|+2\ge 2>0\) and the LHS can never vanish. Equivalently, putting \(t=|x|\ge 0\) gives \(t^{2}+3t+2=(t+1)(t+2)=0\Rightarrow t=-1,-2\), both rejected since \(t\ge 0\). Hence zero real roots.

working: Coefficients are real, so the conjugate \(2-i\sqrt{3}\) is the other root. Sum \(=4=-p\Rightarrow p=-4\); product \(=(2)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}=4+3=7=q\). So \((p,q)=(-4,7)\). Check: \(x^{2}-4x+7\) at \(x=2+i\sqrt{3}\) gives \((1+4i\sqrt{3})-(8+4i\sqrt{3})+7=0\).

For \(2x^{2}-2(k-2)x-(k+1)=0\): \(\alpha+\beta=k-2\), \(\alpha\beta=-(k+1)/2\). Then \(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=(k-2)^{2}+(k+1)=k^{2}-3k+5\), a upward parabola in \(k\) minimised at \(k=3/2\) (value \(11/4\)). Roots stay real for all \(k\) since \(\Delta=4(k^{2}-2k+6)>0\). Hence \(k=3/2\).

\(6x^{2}-5x+1=0\Rightarrow x=1/2,1/3\), so \(\alpha+\beta=5/6\), \(\alpha\beta=1/6<1\). Then \(\tan^{-1}\alpha+\tan^{-1}\beta=\tan^{-1}\frac{\alpha+\beta}{1-\alpha\beta}=\tan^{-1}\frac{5/6}{5/6}=\tan^{-1}1=\pi/4\) (no \(\pi\) correction needed since \(\alpha\beta<1\) and both roots positive).

\(\frac{1-i}{1+i}=\frac{(1-i)^{2}}{(1+i)(1-i)}=\frac{-2i}{2}=-i\). Powers: \((-i)^{1}=-i\) (negative imaginary part), \((-i)^{2}=-1\) (real), \((-i)^{3}=i\) — purely imaginary with POSITIVE imaginary part. Smallest such \(n=3\).

\(|z|=1\Rightarrow z=e^{i\theta}\), and \(1+\bar{z}=\overline{1+z}\). For \(w=1+z\), \(\arg(w/\bar{w})=2\arg w\). Since \(1+e^{i\theta}=2\cos(\theta/2)e^{i\theta/2}\), \(\arg(1+z)=\theta/2\), so the required argument \(=2\cdot\theta/2=\theta\). Numeric check \(\theta=\pi/2\): \((1+i)/(1-i)=i\), \(\arg=\pi/2=\theta\).

working: With \(\theta=\pi/8\): \(1+\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=2\cos^{2}(\theta/2)+2i\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)=2\cos(\theta/2)e^{i\theta/2}\), and the denominator is its conjugate \(2\cos(\theta/2)e^{-i\theta/2}\). Ratio \(=e^{i\theta}\), so the 8th power \(=e^{8i\pi/8}=e^{i\pi}=-1\).

\(z=\frac{\sqrt{3}+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}=\frac{(\sqrt{3}+i)^{2}}{3+1}=\frac{2+2\sqrt{3}i}{4}=\frac{1+\sqrt{3}i}{2}\), which lies in the first quadrant with \(\tan(\arg z)=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \arg z=\pi/3\). (Also directly: \(\arg=\pi/6-(-\pi/6)=\pi/3\).)

A is the graph of \(y=e^{x}\), B the graph of \(y=x\). Common points need \(e^{x}=x\); but \(f(x)=e^{x}-x\) has \(f'(x)=e^{x}-1=0\) at \(x=0\) with minimum \(f(0)=1>0\), so \(e^{x}>x\) for all real \(x\) and the graphs never meet. Hence \(A\cap B=\Phi\) (and neither is a subset of the other, since each is a distinct curve).

working: Count ordered pairs \((A,B)\) with \(A\cap B=\Phi\): each of the 4 elements independently goes to A, to B, or to neither \(\Rightarrow 3^{4}=81\). Only one of these has \(A=B\) (both empty), so the remaining 80 pair up into 40 unordered pairs; adding \(\{\Phi,\Phi\}\) gives \(40+1=41\).

Reflexive: (1,1),(2,2),(3,3) all present. Symmetric: (1,2) is in R but (2,1) is not, so NOT symmetric. Transitive: the only chains are (1,2)+(2,3)\(\to\)(1,3) present, (1,2)+(2,2)\(\to\)(1,2), (2,3)+(3,3)\(\to\)(2,3), (1,3)+(3,3)\(\to\)(1,3) — all present, so R IS transitive. Therefore only "reflexive but not symmetric" is true (B and C and D are false).

working: Domain = those x in {2,3,4,5} having at least one coprime y in {3,6,7,10}: x=2 with y=3 (gcd 1); x=3 with y=7; x=4 with y=3; x=5 with y=3. All four qualify, so domain \(=\{2,3,4,5\}\).

working: Require \(\frac{a^{n+1}+b^{n+1}}{a^{n}+b^{n}}=\frac{a+b}{2}\) for all \(a,b\). Trying \(n=0\): LHS \(=\frac{a+b}{1+1}=\frac{a+b}{2}\) — identity holds. (Check others: \(n=1\) gives \(\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{a+b}\ne\frac{a+b}{2}\) e.g. \(a=1,b=3\Rightarrow 10/4\ne 2\); \(n=-1\) gives the HM \(\frac{2ab}{a+b}\).) So \(n=0\).

For \(x^{2}-10x+11=0\): \(\alpha+\beta=10\), \(\alpha\beta=11\). HM \(=\frac{2\alpha\beta}{\alpha+\beta}=\frac{22}{10}=\frac{11}{5}\).

working: \((1+\alpha x)^{4}\) has 5 terms, middle is the 3rd: \(\binom{4}{2}\alpha^{2}=6\alpha^{2}\). \((1-\alpha x)^{6}\) has 7 terms, middle is the 4th: \(\binom{6}{3}(-\alpha)^{3}=-20\alpha^{3}\). Equating: \(6\alpha^{2}=-20\alpha^{3}\Rightarrow \alpha\ne 0,\ 6=-20\alpha\Rightarrow \alpha=-\frac{3}{10}\). Check: \(6(9/100)=0.54\) and \(-20(-27/1000)=0.54\).
